resources.string: A copy of your games for the Blizzard app

Copies everything you would hate to rebuild or lose into a folder you pick: your game clients, the realms with their characters and settings, and the app\'s choices. The Blizzard app imports it from there, so nothing has to be set up again and no progress is lost. It is only a copy: nothing in this app is moved, changed or deleted.
Left out, because the Blizzard app makes it again
Logs, running-server files, the game\'s Windows runtime, caches and half-finished downloads or imports. Each is listed in the export\'s export.json.

%1$d names can\'t be kept exactly on shared storage (names that differ only in capital letters, or with characters it doesn\'t allow). They are stored under safe names and listed in the export, so the Blizzard app puts them back as they were.
Not in the app\'s storage, so not copied: %1$s.
Free space needed at the destination: up to %1$s (what is already there from an earlier try is skipped).
The folder you picked has %1$s free.
The folder you picked doesn\'t say how much space it has; the export stops with a message if it runs out.
A realm is running (%1$s). Its database must be stopped before it is copied, so the copy is clean. Stopping saves the characters. Stop it and export?
A game is open. Close the game first, then export.
Another job (an import, an install or a download) is running. Wait for it to finish, then export.
A realm is running (%1$s). Stop it first, then export.
Couldn\'t stop %1$s. Stop it in its Server screen and try again; nothing was copied from a running database.
Not enough free space at the destination: it needs %1$s and has %2$s. Free some up or pick another folder, and run it again: what was copied carries on.
The copy stopped: %1$s Run it again: what was already copied is skipped and it carries on.
Stopped before the end. Run it again to carry on: what was already copied is skipped.
Checking the copy against its checksums
Exported %1$d files (%2$s) to %3$s/WoW-export. The originals in this app are untouched. Open the Blizzard app and import from that folder.
The copy is intact: all %1$d files (%2$s) are there and match their checksums.
The copy has problems: %1$d missing, %2$d the wrong size, %3$d not matching their checksums. Run the export again to repair it: the bad files are copied again.
